questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How computers were invented in the 1950s
Why children should play fewer video games and do more sport
Competitive gaming becoming a big sport and business
How to plan a two-week holiday
questions.why: They discuss eSports, the Fortnite phenomenon, and gaming becoming 'a multi-billion-dollar industry'.

questions.q: What does Catherine say about Fortnite?
options: It is very competitive, and you can even hire a coach
It is only popular in Australia
It is an old game from the 1950s
It is too violent for children to play without their parents
questions.why: She says it's very competitive, and 'you can even hire people to be your Fortnite coach'.

questions.q: What is being discussed for eSports?
options: Banning them for under-18s
Including them in the Olympic Games
Showing them only on TV
Making them free to watch
questions.why: Neil says 'they are even discussing including them in the Olympic Games'.

questions.q: When did 13-year-old Kyle Jackson start playing competitively?
options: When he was five
Last year
When he was thirteen and joined a team
When he was around nine or ten
questions.why: Kyle says 'I started playing competitively when I was around nine or ten.'

questions.q: What does Kyle Jackson think he could do?
options: Design his own games
Become a gaming coach
Play at a professional level
Stop playing and study instead
questions.why: He says he could probably go to a pro level if he keeps playing at his current level.

questions.q: What does Catherine think about Kyle saying he's played games 'all his life'?
options: It might be a bit of an exaggeration
It is completely true
It is impossible to believe
It is a sad situation
questions.why: She says 'that might be a little exaggeration', but he's probably played as long as he can remember.

A group of game designers who work together on new games
A TV programme about gaming
A team of players who compete in eSports
questions.why: Neil says Team Secret are like a regular sports team, with players who play matches in eSports.

questions.q: What parts of the gaming industry does George Yao mention?
options: Only playing in competitions
Making and publishing games, and the eSports scene
Selling computers, phones and games consoles around the world
Training coaches and referees
questions.why: He lists production of games, publishing of games and the eSports scene.
